title_en: Judges Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is enacted in accordance with the Constitution for the purposes of comprehensively promoting the construction of a high-quality judge team, strengthening the management and supervision of judges, protecting the lawful rights and interests of judges, ensuring that the People's Courts independently exercise adjudicative power according to law, ensuring that judges perform their duties according to law, and ensuring judicial impartiality.

Article 2 Judges are the adjudicative personnel who exercise the state's adjudicative power according to law, including the presidents, vice-presidents, members of the adjudication committee, division chiefs, deputy division chiefs, and judges of the Supreme People's Court, local People's Courts at various levels, and special People's Courts such as military courts.
Article 3 Judges must faithfully implement the Constitution and laws, uphold social fairness and justice, and serve the people wholeheartedly.
Article 4 Judges shall treat parties and other participants in proceedings impartially, and shall apply the law equally to all persons and organizations.
Article 5 Judges shall be diligent and responsible, honest and upright, and adhere to professional ethics.
Article 6 In adjudicating cases, judges shall base their judgments on facts, take law as the criterion, and uphold an objective and impartial stance.
Article 7 Judges performing their duties according to law shall be protected by law and shall not be subject to interference from administrative organs, social organizations, or individuals.

Article 9 Presidents, vice-presidents, members of the adjudication committee, division chiefs, and deputy division chiefs of the People's Courts shall, in addition to performing their adjudicative duties, also perform duties commensurate with their positions.

Article 14 The method of examination and assessment shall be adopted for first-instance judges, and candidates shall be selected from among those who meet the judge conditions based on the standard of both moral integrity and professional competence.
The president of a People's Court shall have legal professional knowledge and legal professional experience. Vice-presidents and members of the adjudication committee shall be selected from among judges, prosecutors, or other persons who meet the judge conditions.

Article 15 A People's Court may, based on the needs of adjudicative work, openly select judges from lawyers, legal educators, researchers, and other persons engaged in the legal profession.
In addition to meeting the conditions for serving as a judge, lawyers participating in the open selection shall have actually practiced for no less than five years, with rich experience and good professional reputation; legal educators and researchers participating in the open selection shall have intermediate or above professional titles, have engaged in teaching or research for more than five years, and have outstanding research capabilities and corresponding research achievements.

Article 16 Provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall establish judge selection committees, responsible for reviewing the professional competence of first-instance judge candidates.
The composition of the provincial judge selection committee shall include representatives of judges from local People's Courts at various levels, other persons engaged in the legal profession, and relevant parties, with not less than one-third being judges.
The routine work of the provincial judge selection committee shall be undertaken by the internal functional department of the Higher People's Court.
For selecting judges of the Supreme People's Court, a judge selection committee of the Supreme People's Court shall be established, responsible for reviewing the professional competence of judge candidates.

Article 17 First-instance judges shall generally serve in Primary People's Courts. Judges of higher People's Courts shall generally be selected level by level; judges of the Supreme People's Court and Higher People's Courts may be selected from the two lower levels of People's Courts. Judges participating in the selection of a higher People's Court shall have served as judges in a lower People's Court for a certain number of years and have work experience related to the selected position.

Article 18 The appointment and removal of judges shall be handled in accordance with the authority and procedures for appointment and removal prescribed by the Constitution and laws.
The President of the Supreme People's Court shall be elected and removed by the National People's Congress; the Vice-Presidents, members of the Adjudication Committee, division chiefs, deputy division chiefs, and judges shall be appointed and removed by the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress upon the recommendation of the President.
The division chiefs and deputy division chiefs of the circuit courts of the Supreme People's Court shall be appointed and removed by the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress upon the recommendation of the President.
The presidents of local People's Courts at various levels shall be elected and removed by the People's Congress at the corresponding level; the vice-presidents, members of the adjudication committee, division chiefs, deputy division chiefs, and judges shall be appointed and removed by the Standing Committee of the People's Congress at the corresponding level upon the recommendation of the president.
The presidents of Intermediate People's Courts established within districts in provinces and autonomous regions and within municipalities directly under the Central Government shall be appointed and removed by the Standing Committee of the People's Congress of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government based on the nomination of the presidium; the vice-presidents, members of the adjudication committee, division chiefs, deputy division chiefs, and judges shall be appointed and removed by the Standing Committee of the People's Congress of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government upon the recommendation of the president of the Higher People's Court.
The presidents, vice-presidents, members of the adjudication committee, division chiefs, deputy division chiefs, and judges of the People's Courts at various levels of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps and special People's Courts shall be appointed and removed in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress.
Article 19 After judges are produced in accordance with statutory procedures, they shall publicly take an oath to the Constitution at the time of taking office.

Article 21 Where the appointment of a judge is found to have violated the conditions prescribed in this Law, the appointing authority shall revoke such appointment; where a higher People's Court discovers that the appointment of a judge by a lower People's Court violates the conditions prescribed in this Law, it shall recommend that the lower People's Court request the appointing authority to revoke such appointment according to law.

Article 22 A judge shall not concurrently serve as a member of the Standing Committee of the People's Congress, shall not concurrently hold a position in an administrative organ, supervisory organ, or procuratorial organ, shall not concurrently hold a position in an enterprise or other for-profit organization, or a public institution, and shall not concurrently serve as a lawyer, arbitrator, or notary.

Article 25 Judges shall be managed under a post quota system. The judge quota shall be determined based on factors such as the number of cases, economic and social development, population, and the level of the People's Court, and shall be subject to aggregate control and dynamic management within the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government, with priority given to the needs of Primary People's Courts and People's Courts with a high volume of cases.
Where a vacancy arises in the judge quota, it shall be filled promptly in accordance with procedures.
The judge quota of the Supreme People's Court shall be determined by the Supreme People's Court in consultation with relevant departments.

Article 26 Judges shall be managed under a separate rank sequence.
The grades of judges are divided into twelve levels, which are, in descending order: Chief Justice, Grand Justice Grade One, Grand Justice Grade Two, Senior Justice Grade One, Senior Justice Grade Two, Senior Justice Grade Three, Senior Justice Grade Four, Justice Grade One, Justice Grade Two, Justice Grade Three, Justice Grade Four, and Justice Grade Five.
Article 27 The President of the Supreme People's Court shall be the Chief Justice.

Article 28 The determination of a judge's grade shall be based on the judge's moral integrity and professional competence, level of expertise, actual performance in adjudication work, and length of service, among other factors.
The promotion of a judge's grade shall adopt a combination of regular promotion and selective promotion based on merit; judges who are exceptionally outstanding or whose frontline case-handling positions have special needs may be specially selected for promotion.
Article 29 The specific measures for the establishment, determination, and promotion of judges' grades shall be separately prescribed by the State.
Article 30 A unified pre-service training system shall be implemented for newly appointed judges.

Article 31 Judges shall receive planned training in politics, theory, and professional skills.
Training for judges shall integrate theory with practice, be tailored to needs, and emphasize practical results.
Article 32 The training received by a judge shall serve as one of the bases for the judge's appointment and grade promotion.
Article 33 Judge training institutions shall undertake the task of training judges in accordance with relevant regulations.

Article 34 Where a judge applies for resignation, the judge shall submit a written application, and after approval, the judge's position shall be removed in accordance with the procedures prescribed by law.

Article 35 Where a judge is dismissed, the judge's position shall be removed in accordance with the procedures prescribed by law.
The dismissal of a judge shall be decided according to the management authority. The dismissal decision shall be notified in writing to the dismissed judge, and shall state the reasons and basis for the decision.

Article 36 Within two years after leaving a People's Court, a judge shall not act as litigation agent or defender in the capacity of a lawyer.
After leaving a People's Court, a judge shall not act as litigation agent or defender in cases handled by the People's Court where the judge previously served, unless acting as a guardian or close relative of a party to conduct the litigation or defense.
After being expelled, a judge shall not act as litigation agent or defender, unless acting as a guardian or close relative of a party to conduct the litigation or defense.

Article 37 Where necessary for work, a judge may, upon selection or approval by the unit, assist in conducting practical teaching and research activities in institutions of higher education or scientific research institutes, and shall comply with the relevant regulations of the State.
Article 38 A People's Court shall establish a Judge Evaluation Committee, which shall be responsible for the assessment of the judges of that court.

Article 39 The Judge Evaluation Committee shall be composed of five to nine members.
The Director of the Judge Evaluation Committee shall be the President of the court.
Article 40 The assessment of judges shall be comprehensive, objective, and fair, and shall combine routine assessment with annual assessment.

Article 41 The assessment of judges shall include: actual performance in adjudication, professional ethics, professional competence, work ability, and adjudication style. The emphasis shall be on assessing actual performance in adjudication.

Article 42 The annual assessment results shall be divided into four grades: excellent, competent, basically competent, and incompetent.
The assessment results shall serve as the basis for adjusting a judge's rank and salary, as well as for rewards, punishments, removal from office, demotion, and dismissal.
Article 43 The assessment results shall be notified to the judge in writing. If a judge has any objection to the assessment result, he or she may apply for a review.
Article 44 A judge who has outstanding achievements and contributions in adjudication, or who has other prominent deeds, shall be given a reward.

Article 47 Where a judge is suspected of violating discipline or law and has been placed on file for investigation or criminal investigation, and it is inappropriate for him or her to continue to perform duties, his or her performance of duties shall be temporarily suspended in accordance with the authority of management and the prescribed procedures.

Article 48 The Supreme People's Court and provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall establish judicial disciplinary committees, which shall be responsible for reviewing and determining from a professional perspective whether a judge has committed acts violating adjudication duties as specified in items (4) and (5) of Article 46 of this Law, and shall put forward review opinions on whether the judge has intentionally violated duties, committed gross negligence, committed ordinary negligence, or has not violated duties. After the judicial disciplinary committee puts forward its review opinion, the People's Court shall, in accordance with relevant provisions, make a decision on whether to impose a disciplinary sanction and shall take corresponding action.
A judicial disciplinary committee shall be composed of representatives of judges, other persons engaged in legal professions, and representatives from relevant parties, with judges representing no less than half of the members.
The day-to-day work of the Judicial Disciplinary Committee of the Supreme People's Court and the provincial judicial disciplinary committees shall be undertaken by the internal functional departments of the relevant People's Courts.

Article 49 When a judicial disciplinary committee deliberates on disciplinary matters, the judge concerned shall have the right to apply for the withdrawal of relevant persons, and shall have the right to make statements, present evidence, and provide explanations.

Article 50 The review opinions made by the judicial disciplinary committee shall be served on the judge concerned. If the judge concerned has an objection to the review opinion, he or she may raise it with the disciplinary committee, and the disciplinary committee shall review the objection and its reasons and make a decision.

Article 51 The specific procedures for the judicial disciplinary committee to deliberate on disciplinary matters shall be determined by the Supreme People's Court in consultation with relevant departments.
Article 52 People's Courts shall establish judge rights protection committees to safeguard the lawful rights and interests of judges and ensure that judges perform their duties according to law.

Article 54 No unit or individual may require a judge to engage in matters beyond the scope of his or her statutory duties.
For any act that interferes with a judge's handling of cases, the judge shall have the right to refuse it and to fully and truthfully record and report it; if there is a violation of discipline or law, the relevant organ shall, in light of the severity of the circumstances, investigate the liability of the responsible persons and the actors.

Article 55 The professional dignity and personal safety of judges shall be protected by law.
No unit or individual may retaliate against a judge or his or her close relatives.
For illegal or criminal acts such as retaliation, false accusation, insult, defamation, violent assault, threat, intimidation, harassment, or disturbance against a judge or his or her close relatives, a stricter punishment shall be imposed according to law.

Article 56 Where a judge suffers false reporting, false accusation, framing, insult, or defamation due to performing duties according to law, thereby damaging his or her reputation, the People's Court shall, together with relevant departments, promptly clarify the facts, eliminate the adverse effects, and investigate the liability of the relevant unit or individual according to law.

Article 57 Where a judge, due to performing duties according to law, faces danger to the personal safety of himself or herself or his or her close relatives, the People's Court and the public security organ shall take necessary protective measures, such as personal protection and prohibiting specific persons from contacting the judge or his or her close relatives.

Article 58 Judges shall implement a salary system commensurate with their duties, enjoy the salary treatment prescribed by the State according to their judge grades, and establish a mechanism for simultaneous adjustment with the salaries of civil servants.
The salary system for judges shall be separately prescribed by the State based on the characteristics of adjudication work.

Article 59 Judges shall implement a system of regular salary increases.
Those who are assessed as excellent or competent in the annual assessment may have their salary grades raised in accordance with regulations.
Article 60 Judges shall enjoy the allowances, subsidies, bonuses, insurance, and welfare benefits prescribed by the State.

Article 61 A judge who is disabled in the line of duty shall enjoy the disability benefits provided by the state. If a judge is sacrificed, dies in the line of duty, or dies of illness, his or her family members shall enjoy the pensions and preferential treatment provided by the state.
Article 62 The retirement system for judges shall be separately prescribed by the state based on the characteristics of trial work.
Article 63 After retirement, a judge shall enjoy the pension and other benefits provided by the state.
Article 64 Where a state organ or its staff member violates a judge's rights as provided in Article 11 of this Law, the judge shall have the right to lodge a complaint.

Article 65 Where a disciplinary or personnel action against a judge is wrongful, it shall be corrected in a timely manner; if it causes damage to reputation, the judge's reputation shall be rehabilitated, the impact shall be eliminated, and an apology shall be made; if it causes economic losses, compensation shall be made. The directly responsible persons who retaliate shall be investigated for liability according to law.

Article 66 The state shall implement a unified legal professional qualification examination system for newly-appointed judges, which shall be organized and implemented by the judicial administration department of the State Council in consultation with the Supreme People's Court and other relevant departments.

Article 67 A judge assistant of a People's Court shall be responsible for reviewing case materials, drafting legal documents, and other trial auxiliary affairs under the guidance of a judge.
A People's Court shall strengthen the construction of the judge assistant team to reserve talents for the selection of judges.

Article 68 Where provisions on judges' rights, obligations, and management systems are already provided in this Law, the provisions of this Law shall apply; where this Law does not provide, the relevant laws and regulations on the management of public servants shall apply.
Article 69 This Law shall come into force as of October 1, 2019.
